back: A grid of the truth table arranged in Gray code so that neighbouring cells differ in one variable; used to simplify logic expressions.
A sequence in which each value differs from the next in one bit (00, 01, 11, 10).

front: Rules for grouping 1s in a K-map
back: Rectangles of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 adjacent cells; may wrap round the edges and corners; may overlap; cover every 1 with the fewest, largest groups.
Keep the variables that stay the same in every cell of the group (inverted if 0); drop the variables that change. OR the terms together.

front: Size of group and variables removed
back: A group of 2^k cells removes k variables (4 cells remove 2).
An input combination that cannot occur or whose output does not matter (X); it may be treated as 0 or 1 to make groups larger.

front: Number of cells in a K-map
back: 2^n cells for n variables: 4 for two variables, 8 for three, 16 for four.
Visual and systematic, quicker, and less likely to miss a simplification.
Cells on opposite edges of the map, and the four corners, are neighbours and can be grouped.
